headline: Hydra-0 uses image-plane action flow as a cross-embodiment world-model and control interface
summary: Hydra-0 maps robot actions into sparse camera-plane trajectories of visible robot or object points, giving heterogeneous embodiments a common visual action representation. The authors train action-flow-conditioned Cosmos 2.5 and Wan2.2 backbones on 2,201.7 hours of multi-embodiment interaction video, report up to 90.4% lower robot-motion error and 60.2% lower object-motion error than an action-conditioned Cosmos 2.5 baseline, preserve policy rankings under open-loop RoboLab replay (Pearson r=0.96, Spearman rho=0.93, 5.7-point MAE), and demonstrate a qualitative inverse-control mode on one real flexible-pipe-bending task.
